_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for tries.

questions.title: Prefix path
questions.code:
Stored words:
cat
car
dog

Paths:
c -> a -> t
c -> a -> r
d -> o -> g
questions.prompt: A trie stores cat, car, and dog. Which first letter path is shared by cat and car?
questions.explanation: Both words start with c, so they share the first trie edge before splitting later.

questions.title: Word ending marker
questions.code:
Stored words:
app
apple

Path:
a -> p -> p -> l -> e
     app ends here
questions.prompt: Why does a trie node need an end-of-word marker?
choices: A prefix can also be a complete word
It keeps letters sorted by score
questions.explanation: Without an end marker, the trie cannot tell whether app is a word or only the start of apple.

questions.title: Missing edge
questions.prompt: A trie has paths for sun and sum. Searching for sad reaches s, then needs a. What happens?
choices: The search fails at the missing a edge
The search starts from the last node
questions.explanation: A missing child edge means no stored word has that prefix path, so the lookup stops.

questions.title: Autocomplete
questions.prompt: For autocomplete with prefix ca, what part of the trie should be explored after reaching ca?
questions.explanation: Autocomplete first walks to the node for the prefix. From there, it collects only complete words below that node, so words outside the prefix path are not included.

questions.title: Prefix count
questions.prompt: What extra field makes prefix counting faster in a trie?
choices: A count of words passing through each node
A random priority at each node
The index of the last array item
questions.explanation: A pass-through count lets a prefix query return the number stored at the prefix node.

questions.title: Character order
questions.prompt: Before inserting words into a simple lowercase trie, what should code do with mixed-case input?
questions.explanation: Consistent normalization keeps A and a from creating two separate paths unless the prompt wants that distinction.

questions.title: Trie tradeoff
questions.prompt: What is the main tradeoff of a trie?
choices: Fast prefix searches can use more memory
It always beats hashing for exact lookup
questions.explanation: A trie spends nodes on character paths so prefix work is quick, but that can cost more memory than a flat set.

questions.title: Prefix mistake
questions.prompt: A search reaches the prefix node for app. What must be checked before returning that app is a word?
choices: Whether that node marks a complete word
questions.explanation: A prefix path alone is not enough. The node must mark the end of a stored word.
